Shri Siddharth Datt - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Gitesh Singh Thakur - Government Advocate
for the State of M.P.
Learned Government Counsel submits that the victim is served.

Heard on I.A.
No.11107 of 2023 second application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant - Ishwar Singh arising out of judgment dated 07.08.2021 delivered in SPL Case No.76 of 2021 by Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012), District Singrauli.
I.A. No.16414 of 2021, first application for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail was dismissed on merits, vide order dated 07.12.2022.

entities.text: Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012), District Singrauli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellant has been convicted and sentence under Section 376 (2)
(i) of IPC to undergo R.I. for ten years with fine of Rs.2000/- and under Section 376 (2) (n) of IPC to undergo R.I. for twelve years with fine of Rs.2000/- with default stipulation.
The prosecution story is found to be proved that on 5.10.2016 the prosecutrix lodged a written complaint to the effect that the appellant was working as an Engineer in the Watershed Project and was living near his house.
The prosecutrix used to go for a coaching in the second floor of the 2 CRA-5396-2021 house.
In the same house, the appellant was living in the first floor and the appellant used to molest her.
On 8th August 2016 at about 6am when the prosecutrix went to coaching, the appellant caught hold of her and committed the offence.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is in custody since nine years, nine months out of twelve years conviction.
The FIR was lodged after two months.
The FIR was lodged after two months of the incident without there being any plausible explanation.
Dr. Priyanka Gautam (PW-14) and mother of the prosecutrix Smt. Muniya Panika (PW-3) have not supported the case of the prosecution.
No independent witness is available in this case.
At the time of the incident, the prosecutrix was eighteen years of age.
The trial court failed to assess the age of the prosecutrix correctly.

sentences.text: Learned Government Counsel opposed the prayer for suspension of remaining jail sentence on the basis of objection.
He submits that vide order dated 7.5.2022, the application for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail was dismissed on merits and there is no change in the circumstance.

Considering the period of custody of the appellant and conviction and the fact that this appeal being of 2021 cannot be heard in near future, without expressing any conclusive opinion on the merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 11107 of 2023 is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the 3 CRA-5396-2021 remaining jail sentence of this appellant is hereby suspended and it is directed that appellant- Ishwar Singh be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, District Singrauli on 1st May 2025 and also on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
Certified copy as per Rules.
(SUSHRUT ARVIND DHARMADHIKARI)

(AVANINDRA KUM  JUDGE JUDGE  bks Ishwar Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65398775/
